summary.intent: Investigate and fix someguy v0.11.1 IPNS routing failures on staging (endpoints hanging indefinitely), then deploy the fix to staging with proper monitoring and a delegated-ipfs.dev fallback.
summary.outcome: Someguy was fixed with corrected resource limits and DHT configuration, deployed to staging successfully with a working fallback mechanism and Prometheus metrics. Additionally, a long-running release-please tagging deadlock was finally resolved by switching to component-prefixed tags (`cipher-box-v*`) and fixing the staging tag format.

repo: Someguy IPNS routing requires: libp2p port 4004 exposed (TCP+UDP), DHT mode set to 'accelerated', minimum 2GB RAM / 1 CPU, connection limits 100/3000, and SOMEGUY_LIBP2P_MAX_MEMORY must be a raw uint64 byte count (e.g. 1073741824), not a human-readable string like '1GB'

The delegated routing client in ipns.service.ts resolves from both network and DB then picks the higher sequence number — since DB is written synchronously before DHT publish, the DB always wins, so 100% of resolves come from the database by design
Vitest does not auto-load .env files into process.env; env vars must be passed explicitly (e.g. SDK_E2E_THROTTLE_BYPASS_SECRET=xxx pnpm exec vitest)
The ThrottlerBypassGuard uses an x-throttle-bypass header checked against THROTTLE_BYPASS_SECRET, not NODE_ENV=test

Release-please multi-package Merge plugin produces PR titles like 'chore: release main' (no version) and 'include-component-in-tag: false' is broken for the root package in multi-package mode — release scanner cannot match bare v{version} tags back to path '.'
Release-please deadlocks when it finds a merged release PR with 'autorelease: pending' label: it aborts with 'untagged, merged release PRs outstanding' instead of tagging it

Staging GitHub Releases with old format 'v{version}-staging-rc-{n}' were parsed by release-please as component 'staging' and collided with root package tag scanning, causing it to walk 600+ commit history
The THROTTLE_BYPASS_SECRET was not wired into the staging deploy workflow, meaning it would be lost on every redeploy

code.finding: Rewrote to support primary/fallback backends: primary (someguy) is tried with full retry logic, fallback (delegated-ipfs.dev) only triggered after primary exhausts all retries. Prometheus counters track per-backend request outcomes.
backend parameter typed as 'primary' | 'fallback' union instead of string — PR review comment from Copilot
Two new Prometheus counters added: cipherbox_delegated_routing_requests_total{operation,backend,outcome} and cipherbox_delegated_routing_fallbacks_total{operation}
Someguy healthcheck must use 'curl -sf' not 'wget -qO-' — someguy image ships curl but not wget (confirmed via docker exec)

Root package needs 'include-component-in-tag: true' with component 'cipher-box' to produce 'cipher-box-v{version}' tags. Without this, release-please creates bare 'v{version}' tags but its own scanner cannot match them back to path '.' in multi-package mode.

workflow: Load test comparison (someguy vs delegated-ipfs.dev): someguy has ~40% higher median latency but ~20% lower p99 (more predictable); delegated-ipfs.dev is faster at median but higher variance. Both zero errors at tested load levels.

Release-please anchor releases must be created manually when bootstrapping a new package or recovering from a broken state — the release must point to the correct commit SHA and match the expected tag format exactly

When release-please creates a release PR but fails to tag it, the label must be manually flipped from 'autorelease: pending' to 'autorelease: tagged' after manually creating the tag, otherwise it will deadlock on the next run

Staging GitHub Releases (containing desktop build artifacts) should not be created under 'v*' tag prefixes — use a format that release-please won't parse as a component (staging-v* was still parsed as component 'staging'; consider omitting GitHub Releases for staging builds entirely)
The 1Password SSH agent requires interactive approval for each SSH session; automated scripts that require VPS access will fail without prior approval

friction: release-please has a fundamental bug: 'include-component-in-tag: false' for the root package in multi-package mode creates bare 'v{version}' tags but the scanner cannot match them back to path '.' — required switching to component-prefixed tags after extensive debugging
Multiple release-please deadlocks due to merged PRs with 'autorelease: pending' labels requiring manual intervention (label flip + manual tag creation) at least 4 times during the session
Old-format staging releases (v{version}-staging-rc-{n}) were silently corrupting release-please's release scanner — 29 historical releases had to be deleted
SOMEGUY_LIBP2P_MAX_MEMORY silently fails with human-readable strings like '1GB' — container crash-looped on staging with no obvious error until SSH investigation
1Password SSH agent blocks automated VPS SSH commands, requiring manual approval or workarounds
Web E2E tests on main are flaky, blocking auto-merge of release PRs multiple times
The release-please label race condition on PR creation (label API call fires before GitHub resolves the PR node ID) caused a spurious failure requiring manual label addition
Vitest doesn't auto-load .env files, causing 429s in SDK E2E tests until env vars were passed explicitly — wasted time debugging throttler configuration
open_items: packages/crypto is now tracked by release-please independently but has no historical releases — first release will include all accumulated commits since repo start
DB-first IPNS resolution means someguy/DHT provides no latency benefit for API clients; reducing DB dependency would require changing resolve logic to prefer network when sequence numbers match

Staging GitHub Releases containing desktop build artifacts (Tauri) are still parsed by release-please as component 'staging' — causes a warning each run; consider not creating GitHub Releases for staging builds
THROTTLE_BYPASS_SECRET was added to deploy-staging.yml but that change needs to be committed and included in the next release
Someguy fallback metrics (cipherbox_delegated_routing_fallbacks_total) are not yet wired into Grafana dashboards or alerts — needs panel and alert rule creation
Mock IPNS routing service is still in docker-compose.yml alongside someguy — kept for CI isolation but adds cognitive overhead
The someguy sidecar DHT routing table was freshly started during load testing — median latency gap vs delegated-ipfs.dev should narrow after the DHT warms up on staging
